Automated hardness testing system with robot
Automated hardness testing system with robot
Modular design, expandable with additional test systems
The hardness testing station has a modular design and, according to requirements, can be supplemented by sample processing stations or additional test systems (e.g. geometric measurement or determination of the surface roughness). This means motor blocks, steel or aluminum rims and even housing parts can be tested. It is possible to adapt the system to the special requirements of every single customer at any time.
 The robot takes over the central handling tasks between individual testing stations that previously required a high amount of time and manpower. Also, any faults that occur within the framework of the manual testing are eliminated. According to requirements, the automatic hardness testing centre works using the Vickers, Rockwell or Brinell procedure. This reliably tests a wide range of materials for their hardness, according to the respective requirements. The hardness tester module can be replaced or supplemented by a universal testing machine if required, depending on the modular system implemented. In this case, fully automated tensile, pressure and bending tests can be conducted.
 A system also consists of following components: 
hardness tester with an integrated, fully automatic optical system (up to 3000 kp) 
robots designed for test objects with a weight up to 120 kg 
sample preparation station (milling machine) 
identification station for collecting information on component markings using a camera system 
marking station for marking the components 
feeding and magazining units

 Hardness testers and hardness testing machines 
 Hardness testers and Hardness testing machines
The Brinell-Vickers and Rockwell hardness testing methods are frequently used in the mechanical testing of metals and are an integral part of industrial quality assurance. Hegewald & Peschke MPT GmbH offers a broad portfolio of hardness testers for a wide variety of applications: 
Semi- or fully automatic micro and small load hardness testers (e.g. series HP10/30) for characterization of hardness gradients, weld seams, etc.  
Universal Brinell-Vickers-Rockwell Macro Hardness Tester (e.g. series HPuniversal) for industrial application 
Automated hardness testing systems integrated into the production process with component feeding 
We offer the appropriate test accessories, universal hardness testing software and the possibility of modernising older hardness testers to match the various hardness testers. 
Automated hardness testing solutions are tailored to the respective operational requirements in close cooperation with the customer.
 Hardness measurement on a mechanical component made of brass with universal hardness tester HPuniversal
Each of our hardness testers guarantees highest accuracy, reliability, safe measurement and a long service life. Our service guarantees comprehensive technical and application support after installation. This also includes the possibility of DAkkS calibration for the Brinell-Vickers and Rockwell methods.
To complement our product portfolio in the field of portable and Rockwell hardness testers, we cooperate with CISAM-Ernst. CISAM-Ernst is a leading hardness testing company with more than 60 years of experience in the research, development and manufacture of hardness testers.

 Automated testing systems 
 Automation
 Fully automated testing system for tensile tests on shoulder head specimens
Metal- and plastic-processing companies with high testing amount more and more often count on fully automatic testing plants and the advantages linked with it: The efficiency of the machines is raised as well as the personnel expenditure and the testing costs are reduced.
Hegewald & Peschke MPT GmbH offers complete engineering solutions in the area of destructive material testing on the basis of universal testing machines and hardness testers. The heart of these plants is usually a handling system based on an industrial robot. The whole testing process is controlled and supervised by the universal material testing software LabMaster. Via a remote diagnostic system the necessary high availability of the plants is safeguarded.
Make a request for automated test systems
Fully automated and partially automated test systems
Test cells can be supplied in different versions in terms of the degree of automation.
In the fully automated process, the specimens in the test cell are identified via an ID and the test sequences are controlled by information from the network. In (partially) automated test cells, on the other hand, the tester performs specimen identification or a manual selective follow-up check, for example. In both variants, processes such as specimen measurement, labeling and other test-specific tasks can be integrated into the automated process.
Advantages of fully automated testing systems: 
Integration directly into the production process 
Very high specimen throughput possible 
No qualified operator required for specimen feeding and system operation 
Advantages of partially automated test cells: 
Easy integration into the test laboratory workflow 
Specimen identification by tester 
Support of routine processes in the test laboratory and thus relief for test personnel 
Can be converted for other testing tasks
